description:
BLOCKED on the wide-boiling solver gap — see the sibling bug bead.

Configuration code is WRITTEN and compiles: CrudeColumnConfig (stages, feed stage, pressure, reflux, bottoms, liquid side draws), CrudeColumnError with five specific validation rejections, CutResult/CrudeColumnResult, and solve_crude_column wiring the slate through RigorousColumn with Stage::with_side_draws. Config validation and material balance are tested and pass.

What does NOT work is the solve itself. The end-to-end test is committed #[ignore]d with the full diagnosis in its doc comment rather than deleted or quietly loosened, so the failure is visible to the next reader.

Decision made and recorded in CrudeColumnConfig's docs: this is a REBOILED column, not the refluxed-absorber-with-stripping-steam a real CDU is. ColumnType::RefluxedAbsorber exists in the enum but RigorousColumn::distillation() is the only constructor and fixes the type. The consequence — no stripping steam, no pump-arounds, no furnace, so the energy balance is not a refinery's — is stated in the docs rather than hidden.

Resume when the solver gap is addressed.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
WORKS. The crude column converges to a physical, monotonic profile with a realistic cut slate.

38 degAPI crude, 10 pseudo-components, 650 K residue cut point, 12 stages, 3 side draws, RR 3.0, ideal K-values, Wang-Henke: converged in 38 iterations to 6.7e-7.

  stage  0 (overhead) 0.3376 mol/s  423.6 K (150 C)  naphtha
  stage  4            0.0900 mol/s  494.9 K (222 C)  kerosene
  stage  6            0.0750 mol/s  511.7 K (239 C)  kerosene
  stage  8            0.0600 mol/s  530.8 K (258 C)  diesel
  stage 11 (bottoms)  0.4373 mol/s  588.5 K (315 C)  residue

Those land in the conventional CDU bands (overhead 120-150 C, kero 200-250 C, diesel 250-300 C, flash zone 340-370 C) — a sanity agreement, not a validation.

TWO REAL ERRORS were found and fixed, and both had produced a 'converged' answer with a small residual:

1. FEEDING THE COLUMN ITS OWN UNDISTILLABLE HEAVY END. A crude's pseudo-components run past 800 K NBP and cannot vaporise at 1.2 bar. Asking the fractionator to separate them is asking it to separate something with no vapour phase. Fixed by routing everything above a residue cut point around the column straight to the bottoms — which is exactly what a refinery does, and why atmospheric residue goes to a vacuum tower. Measured: cut points 560/650/700 K all converge monotonically in 26-32 iterations; no cut point gives non-monotonic in 79-90.

2. SIDE DRAWS LARGER THAN THE INTERNAL LIQUID. With draws as absolute rates, the bypass shrank the column feed until draws (0.15 mol/s) exceeded internal reflux (0.10 mol/s), draining the column above the feed. Draws are now FRACTIONS of the column feed so they scale with it, and the doc states the reflux_ratio/(1+reflux_ratio) ceiling.

So op-190j.5 needs rewriting: the wide-boiling difficulty was real but it was NOT primarily a solver defect. Two of the three symptoms were my modelling errors. What survives as a genuine gap is the PR78 absence and Wang-Henke reporting success on a non-physical profile.

Also retained from before: this is a REBOILED column, not the refluxed-absorber-with-stripping-steam a real CDU is, and CrudeColumnConfig says so.

title: crude: CDU column configuration with side draws

description:
Recorded as a PROPOSAL. Do not execute a deletion from this bead.

A proposal to delete crates/nee_soon was raised. The numbers behind it were WRONG and the deletion looks unsafe as scoped. Recording the corrected picture so the proposal can be judged honestly.

CLAIMED: 1,005 lines, ~95% doc comment wrapped around two `pub use` statements.
ACTUAL (measured 2026-08-07):
- 1,005 total lines across 7 files (lib.rs 177; xin_wang_sp3_workflow/ mod.rs 204, case.rs 163, sp3_multiphysics.rs 141, mesh_mc.rs 115, mgxs.rs 103, validation.rs 102).
- 490 non-comment non-blank lines -- 49%, NOT ~5%. The claim was off by about an order of magnitude.
- It is not "two pub use statements". Those exist (lib.rs:61-62, re-exporting NordheimFuchsExactTimestepper and TehOPrkeError), but lib.rs:59 also declares `pub mod xin_wang_sp3_workflow;` -- a 6-file, 828-line module with ~40 public items (XinWangSp3Workflow, MgxsGenerationStage, MeshMonteCarloStage, Sp3MultiphysicsStage, Fig429ValidationStage, Mk1DesignPoint, ControlRodRemovalTransient, digitised Fig-4.29 reference curve, 8-group energy structure), plus pub struct NeeSoon (lib.rs:95) and its real pass-through new_prompt_excursion_model (lib.rs:111-129).

WHAT IS fairly criticised: all four workflow stages are stubs returning WorkflowError::NotYetImplemented (mgxs.rs:97-102, mesh_mc.rs:109, sp3_multiphysics.rs:135, validation.rs:96). So it is real STRUCTURE with no physics -- a different and much weaker criticism than "95% comment around two re-exports".

DEPENDENTS (deletion breaks all of these):

- crates/tampines/Cargo.toml:60  <-- a SECOND dependent the workspace CLAUDE.md does not mention; fix that doc gap regardless
- root Cargo.toml:19 (member) and :288 (workspace dep)
- live use in 3 example trees: tampines/examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/prke_backend/mod.rs:5,588; digital-twin-engine/examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/prke_backend/mod.rs:5,588; digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1/{app/schematic.rs:44, physics/kinetics.rs:36}

RECOMMENDATION: do not delete. Either finish the four workflow stages (they belong to the op-fr2.2 Xin Wang SP3 epic) or shrink nee_soon to the re-export shim its dependents actually use -- but that is a decision for the maintainer, not a cleanup.

description:
Batched **golden-section search** (golden-ratio 1-D minimisation) across the
three backends. There is no golden-section implementation in the crate today —
this is new code, in `src/math/` or a new `src/optimise/`.

Why it is wanted: derivative-free bracketed minimisation of a scalar function
on `[a, b]`, for the cases where a root-find is the wrong tool (minimising a
residual, a limiter blend factor, a property-inversion objective that is not
monotone).

What to deliver:

- Serial reference: classic golden-section with the fixed `(3 - sqrt(5)) / 2`
  contraction, a stated bracketing precondition (unimodal on `[a, b]` — say
  loudly in the doc that a non-unimodal input gives *a* local minimum, not
  *the* minimum), and both absolute and relative interval tolerances.
- **Batched** form: N independent brackets contracted in lockstep. Golden
  section is uniformly convergent and branch-free, so this is one of the
  cleanest GPU fits in the whole epic — the interval count after k iterations
  is identical in every lane.
- Optional Brent-style parabolic-interpolation variant as a CPU-only faster
  path; do **not** put it on the GPU, its branching kills the lockstep
  property that makes the batched version worth doing.

V&V: analytic minima of smooth test functions with known answers, plus the
theoretical contraction rate (interval width should shrink by the golden ratio
per iteration — assert it). Record the measured numbers per the workspace V&V
documentation rule.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implementation landed 2026-08-13 (agent session, AI-assisted draft, NO human V&V).

FILES: crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/math/minimise.rs (new),
src/math/minimise/tests.rs (new), src/math/mod.rs (pub mod + pub use only).

Generalised the existing tampines-steam-tables golden_section_max_g rather than
writing a new algorithm; same Price & Robertson (2012) citation, same structure,
same bracket-width stopping rule. One deviation: probe reuse (1 objective
evaluation per iteration instead of 2). tampines-steam-tables was NOT edited --
promotion recommendation filed as op-uyi3.

DELIVERED: golden_section_batch(problems, Sense, MinSettings, ComputeBackend, f);
Sense{Minimise,Maximise}; MinProblem/MinSettings/MinStatus/MinSolution/MinBatch/
MinBatchFailure mirroring math::parallel's Root* vocabulary 1:1;
minimise_backend_for(); GOLDEN_RATIO; SQRT_EPSILON;
MINIMISE_BATCH_MIN_PROBLEMS = 256 (measured).

NOT DELIVERED, deliberately: the optional Brent parabolic variant. Two Brent
minimisers already exist in outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs (petroleum/fitting.rs,
columns/shortcut.rs); a third would be the duplication the CLAUDE.md search rule
forbids. Also no GPU kernel -- Gpu requests degrade to the best CPU path.

MEASURED (release, 4 logical cores, 2026-08-13):
- crossover 256 problems (cheap 1.12x/1.17x, costly 1.55x/2.91x over two runs);
  128 lost on the cheap objective in both runs. Same value as
  math::parallel::ROOT_BATCH_MIN_PROBLEMS -- both compute bound per lane.
- bitwise identical Serial vs CpuMulti at 1/2/4/8 worker threads, 2048 lanes,
  both Sense variants. Asserted, not merely printed.
- accuracy: 1 + (x-x0)^2 -> 1.053671e-8 (sqrt(eps) = 1.490116e-8);
  1 + (x-x0)^4 -> 1.026485e-4 (eps^0.25 = 1.220703e-4), i.e. 9742x worse;
  (x-x0)^2 with a zero minimum value -> 8.881784e-16. The sqrt(eps) floor is a
  property of the OBJECTIVE's relative precision near its extremum, not of
  golden section.
- contraction rate exact to 2.7e-14 relative for k <= 20, degrading to 2.3e-6 at
  k = 80 -- accumulated rounding from probe reuse, absolute effect 4e-22, no
  consequence for any answer. Recorded rather than hidden.

TESTS: 446 lib (--features parallel) / 443 (default) / 83 doctests, all green,
up from 427/425/74. Android aarch64-linux-android --all-targets clean under both
feature settings.

STILL TO DO (maintainer): src/prelude.rs re-export and the README "Ported items"
row -- deliberately left to the maintainer, not done in this session.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Closed as GitHub #12. Same situation as op-yvj.4.2: left In Progress by root@vm on 2026-08-12, claim 22 days stale, work complete on develop.

src/math/minimise.rs (~1400 lines) + 28 tests. Every acceptance criterion met: GOLDEN_RATIO documented with the (3-sqrt(5))/2 equivalence; unimodality precondition stated in three places including that a converged bracket does NOT assert unimodality; both absolute and relative interval tolerances in MinSettings; golden_section_batch contracting N brackets in lockstep with per-lane MinStatus/MinBatchFailure; bracket_contracts_at_the_golden_ratio asserts the theoretical contraction rate directly.

Brent parabolic variant deliberately NOT added — two Brent minimisers already exist in the workspace (outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs petroleum::fitting and columns::shortcut), so a third here would be the duplication the search-before-building rule exists to prevent. Documented with cross-references.

GPU: blocked by the closure boundary, not by effort. golden_section_batch<F> takes a Rust closure. The bead correctly predicted this would be one of the cleanest GPU fits arithmetically — the obstacle is the function-passing mechanism, not the algorithm.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: golden-section (golden-ratio) 1-D minimisation, batched on the hybrid backend
